L'Objectif de ce script est de réaliser une synthèse des résultats obtenue via les analyses des modeles avec les différentes espèces de poissons d'eau douce de la région Bourgogne-Franche-Comte (BFC).

Plan du script 

1. Densite surfacique 

a. **Modèles Linéaires Généralisé Mixtes (GLMM)**

b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  


2. Occurence

a. **Modèles Linéaires Généralisé Mixtes (GLMM)**

<!-- ##b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**   -->

3. Biomasse

a. **Modèles Linéaires Généralisé Mixtes (GLMM)**

<!-- ##b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**   -->



On commence par l'indicateur d'abondance : la densité surfacique.


#1. Densite surfacique 

On importe le jeu de donnée et on fait des ajustement pour avoir toutes les variables avec les bons noms.

```{r}
# preparer la table pour jointure
ope_selection <- ope_selection %>%
  dplyr::select(ope_id, pop_id, sta_id)

# Ajout des coordonnées pour jointure avec df pour future analyse autocorrelation spatiale
coord_sta_id <- point_prelevement %>%
  filter(pop_id %in% pop_serie_tempo) %>%
  rename(x = pop_coordonnees_x, y = pop_coordonnees_y) %>%
  select(pop_id, x, y) %>%
  mutate(pop_id = as.factor(pop_id))

# prepéarer la table pour jointure 
esp_ope_selection_join <- esp_ope_selection %>% 
  select(ope_id, ope_surface_calculee) %>% 
  distinct(ope_id, .keep_all = TRUE)


ope_effectif_glmm_abs <- ope_indicateur %>%
  filter(indicateur == "effectif_total") %>% 
  mef_ajouter_type_protocole() %>% 
  left_join( y= ope_selection, by = c("ope_id", "pop_id", "annee")) %>% 
  inner_join(esp_ope_selection_join, by = "ope_id") %>% 
  mutate(
    valeur = as.numeric(valeur) ,
    annee = as.numeric(annee),
    ope_surface_calculee = as.numeric(ope_surface_calculee),
    pro_libelle = as.factor(pro_libelle),
    pop_id = as.factor(pop_id),
    sta_id = as.factor(sta_id),
    stade = as.factor(stade)
  ) %>%
  left_join(coord_sta_id, by = "pop_id") %>%
  mutate(x = as.numeric(x), y = as.numeric(y)) %>%
  rename(espece = esp_code_alternatif) %>% 
  filter(stade == "ind")
```

## ABLETTE (ABL)

```{r}
data_esp <- ope_effectif_glmm_abs %>% 
  filter(espece == "ABL")
```

###a. **Modèles Linéaires Généralisé Mixtes (GLMM)**

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_zi_1.0 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) +pro_libelle + (1 |
                                                           sta_id) ,
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.1 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.2 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = truncated_poisson(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.3 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
```

On selectionne à l'aide du critère AIC le meilleur modèle c'est à dire le modèle avec le plus petit AIC. 

```{r}
AIC(mod_zi_1.0, mod_zi_1.1, mod_zi_1.2, mod_zi_1.3)
```

Verification de l'ajustement des modèles au données : 
```{r, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 20}
res_mod_zi_1.0 <- as.ggplot(~ plotresid(mod_zi_1.0))
res_mod_zi_1.1 <- as.ggplot(~ plotresid(mod_zi_1.1))
res_mod_zi_1.2 <- as.ggplot(~ plotresid(mod_zi_1.2))
res_mod_zi_1.3 <- as.ggplot(~ plotresid(mod_zi_1.3))

ggarrange(
  res_mod_zi_1.0,
  res_mod_zi_1.1,
  res_mod_zi_1.2,
  res_mod_zi_1.3,
  ncol = 2,
  nrow = 2,
  labels = c("poisson", "nbinom2", "truncated_poisson", "truncated_nbinom2"),
  font.label = list(
    size = 13,
    color = "darkred",
    face = "bold",
    family = NULL
  ),
  hjust = -0.1,
  vjust = 1.6,
  align = c("none", "h", "v", "hv")
)
```

```{r, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 20}

sim_res_mod_zi_1.0 <- as.ggplot(~ plotResiduals(simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_zi_1.0, n = 1000), quantreg = T))
sim_res_mod_zi_1.1 <- as.ggplot(~ plotResiduals(simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_zi_1.1, n = 1000), quantreg = T))
sim_res_mod_zi_1.2 <- as.ggplot(~ plotResiduals(simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_zi_1.2, n = 1000), quantreg = T))
sim_res_mod_zi_1.3 <- as.ggplot(~ plotResiduals(simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_zi_1.3, n = 1000), quantreg = T))

ggarrange(
  sim_res_mod_zi_1.0,
  sim_res_mod_zi_1.1,
  sim_res_mod_zi_1.2,
  sim_res_mod_zi_1.3,
  ncol = 2,
  nrow = 2,
  labels = c("poisson", "nbinom2", "truncated_poisson", "truncated_nbinom2"),
  font.label = list(
    size = 13,
    color = "darkred",
    face = "bold",
    family = NULL
  ),
  hjust = -0.1,
  vjust = 1.6,
  align = c("none", "h", "v", "hv")
)
```

```{r}
DHARMa::testDispersion(mod_zi_1.0, plot = T)
DHARMa::testDispersion(mod_zi_1.1, plot = T)
DHARMa::testDispersion(mod_zi_1.2, plot = T)
DHARMa::testDispersion(mod_zi_1.3, plot = T)

```

Resultats du meilleur modèle : 

```{r}
summary(mod_zi_1.1)
```

```{r}
Anova(mod_zi_1.1)
```


###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  


Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.4 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
var <- variogram(valeur ~ annee + ope_surface_calculee, locations = ~ x+y, data = data_esp)
var
plot(var, col= "black")
```

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

Ajustement des modèles au données :

```{r}
appraise(mod_gamm_1.0)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.1)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.2)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.3)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.4)

```

```{r}
k.check(mod_gamm_1.0)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.1)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.2)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.3)
```


```{r}
res_mod_gamm_1.0 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.0,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.1 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.1,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.2 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.2,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.3 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.3,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
```

```{r}
DHARMa::testDispersion(res_mod_gamm_1.0)
DHARMa::testDispersion(res_mod_gamm_1.1)
DHARMa::testDispersion(res_mod_gamm_1.2)
DHARMa::testDispersion(res_mod_gamm_1.3)

```

```{r}
concurvity(mod_gamm_1.0)
concurvity(mod_gamm_1.1)
concurvity(mod_gamm_1.2)
concurvity(mod_gamm_1.3)
```


```{r}
draw(mod_gamm_1.0, residuals = T)
draw(mod_gamm_1.1, residuals = T)
draw(mod_gamm_1.2, residuals = T)
draw(mod_gamm_1.3, residuals = T)
```


Selection de modèle par l'AIC :

```{r}
AIC(
  # mod_gamm_1.0, 
  # mod_gamm_1.1,
  # mod_gamm_1.2,
  mod_gamm_1.3,
  mod_gamm_1.4
  )
```


Resultats poptrend :

```{r}
trend <- poptrend::ptrend(
  valeur ~ trend(annee, tempRE = F, type = "smooth") + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  bootType = "hessian",
  gamModel = TRUE,
  engine = "gam"
)
# Ajustement du modele
poptrend::checkFit(trend, residuals = T)

summary(trend)
```

```{r}
#Representation graphique du modele
plot(trend, residuals = T)
```

```{r}
# Compute the change in the population over a time interval
poptrend::change(trend, start = 2007 , end = 2025, alpha = 0.05)
```

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,

  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(

  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(

  data = data_esp,

  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.4 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle  + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
var <- variogram(valeur ~ annee + ope_surface_calculee, locations = ~ x+y, data = data_esp)
var
plot(var, col= "black")
```

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.4 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
var <- variogram(valeur ~ annee + ope_surface_calculee, locations = ~ x+y, data = data_esp)
var
plot(var, col= "black")
```

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```



```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
var <- variogram(valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)), locations = ~ x+y, data = data_esp)
var
plot(var, col= "black")
```

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

```{r}
#   data = data_esp,

#   method = "REML"

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(

  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.4 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle  + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
var <- variogram(valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)), locations = ~ x+y, data = data_esp)
var
plot(var, col= "black")
```


```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

Ajustement des modèles au données :

```{r}

appraise(mod_gamm_1.1)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.2)
```

```{r}
                                      plot = TRUE,

res_mod_gamm_1.2 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.2,

                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.3 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.3,
```

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

Ajustement des modèles au données :

```{r}
appraise(mod_gamm_1.0)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.1)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.2)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.3)
```

```{r}
k.check(mod_gamm_1.1)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.2)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.3)
```

```{r}
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.2 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.2,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.3 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.3,

                                      n = 1000)
```

###a. **Modèles Linéaires Généralisé Mixtes (GLMM)**

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_zi_1.0 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) +pro_libelle + (1 |
                                                           sta_id) ,
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.1 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.2 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = truncated_poisson(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.3 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
```

On selectionne à l'aide du critère AIC le meilleur modèle c'est à dire le modèle avec le plus petit AIC.

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

Ajustement des modèles au données :

```{r}

appraise(mod_gamm_1.1)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.2)
```

```{r}
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.2 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.2,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.3 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.3,
```

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

Ajustement des modèles au données :

```{r}

appraise(mod_gamm_1.1)
appraise(mod_gamm_1.2)

```

```{r}
k.check(mod_gamm_1.1)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.2)
k.check(mod_gamm_1.3)
```

```{r}
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.2 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.2,
                                      plot = TRUE,
                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.3 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.3,
```

```{r}
mod_zi_1.0 <- glmmTMB(

)
mod_zi_1.1 <- glmmTMB(

  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.2 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
  family = truncated_poisson(link = "log"),
  data = data_esp,
  ziformula = ~ 1
)
mod_zi_1.3 <- glmmTMB(
  valeur ~ annee + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + (1 | sta_id) ,
```

###b. **Modèles Additifs Généralisé Mixtes (GAMMs)**  

Construire les modèles :

```{r}
mod_gamm_1.0 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.1 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee))  + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "identity"),
  method = "REML"
)
mod_gamm_1.2 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x,y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = poisson(link = "sqrt"),
  method = "REML"
)

mod_gamm_1.3 <- gam(
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

```{r}
appraise(mod_gamm_1.1)
```

```{r}
                                      plot = TRUE,

res_mod_gamm_1.2 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.2,

                                      n = 1000)
res_mod_gamm_1.3 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_gamm_1.3,
```

```{r}
  valeur ~ s(annee) + offset(log(ope_surface_calculee)) + pro_libelle + s(x, y) + s(sta_id, bs = "re"),
  data = data_esp,
  family = nb(link = "log"),
  method = "REML"
)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation temporelle : 

```{r}
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.0, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.1, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.2, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
acf(residuals(mod_gamm_1.3, type = "scaled.pearson"), lag.max = 20)
```

Tester l'autocorrelation spatiale : 

```{r}
show.vgms(models = c("Exp",  # Exponential model
                     "Sph",  # Spherical model
                     "Gau",  # Gaussian model
                     "Nug"), # Nugget model
          nugget = 50)

vfit <- fit.variogram(var, vgm(c("Exp", "Gau", "Sph")))
vfit

# Did the model-fitting process converge successfully?
# This is not guaranteed for nonlinear models.
attributes(vfit)$singular

# For convenience, use show.vgms() to calculate the
# predicted values for our fitted model
fitted <-show.vgms(min = min(var$dist), 
                   max = max(var$dist), 
                   models ="Sph",
                   range = vfit$range[2],
                   sill = vfit$psill[2],
                   nugget = vfit$psill[1],
                   plot = FALSE)

# Now we can easily plot this against the observed data
ggplot(var, aes(dist, gamma)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(data = fitted, 
            aes(distance, semivariance),
            linetype = 2)
```

#2. Occurence
```{r}
# preparer la table pour jointure
ope_selection <- ope_selection %>%
  dplyr::select(ope_id, pop_id, sta_id)

# Ajout des coordonnées pour jointure avec df pour future analyse autocorrelation spatiale
coord_sta_id <- point_prelevement %>%
  filter(pop_id %in% pop_serie_tempo) %>%
  rename(x = pop_coordonnees_x, y = pop_coordonnees_y) %>%
  select(pop_id, x, y) %>%
  mutate(pop_id = as.factor(pop_id))

# prepéarer la table pour jointure 
esp_ope_selection_join <- esp_ope_selection %>% 
  select(ope_id, ope_surface_calculee) %>% 
  distinct(ope_id, .keep_all = TRUE)


ope_occurence_glmm <- ope_indicateur %>%
  filter(indicateur == "occurence") %>% 
  mef_ajouter_type_protocole() %>% 
  left_join( y= ope_selection, by = c("ope_id", "pop_id", "annee")) %>% 
  inner_join(esp_ope_selection_join, by = "ope_id") %>% 
  mutate(
    valeur = as.numeric(valeur) ,
    annee = as.numeric(annee),
    ope_surface_calculee = as.numeric(ope_surface_calculee),
    pro_libelle = as.factor(pro_libelle),
    pop_id = as.factor(pop_id),
    sta_id = as.factor(sta_id),
    stade = as.factor(stade)
  ) %>%
  left_join(coord_sta_id, by = "pop_id") %>%
  mutate(x = as.numeric(x), y = as.numeric(y)) %>%
  rename(espece = esp_code_alternatif) %>% 
  filter(stade == "ind")
```

## TRF 
```{r}
data_esp <- ope_occurence_glmm %>% 
  filter(espece == "ANG")
```

###a. **Modèles Linéaires Généralisé Mixtes (GLMM)**

```{r}
mod_glm_1.0 <- glmer(
  valeur ~ annee  + pro_libelle + (1 |
                                     sta_id) ,
  data = data_esp,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

mod_glm_1.1 <- glmer(
  valeur ~ annee  + pro_libelle + (1 |
                                     sta_id) ,
  data = data_esp,
  family = binomial(link = "probit")
)
mod_glm_1.2 <- glmer(
  valeur ~ annee  + pro_libelle + (1 |
                                     sta_id) ,
  data = data_esp,
  family = binomial(link = "cauchit")
)

mod_glm_1.3 <- glmer(
  valeur ~ annee  + pro_libelle + (1 |
                                     sta_id) ,
  data = data_esp,
  family = binomial(link = "cloglog")
)

```

On selectionne à l'aide du critère AIC le meilleur modèle c'est à dire le modèle avec le plus petit AIC. 

```{r}
AIC(
  mod_glm_1.0,
  mod_glm_1.1,
  mod_glm_1.2,
  mod_glm_1.3
  )
```

Verification de l'ajustement des modèles au données :
